Positioning

Self-care is already social. Very few rooms are built to hold it, and fewer still are licensed to treat you in one.

The problem

Wellness on the Westside is fragmented.

A patient today who wants to optimize their health must book with a plastic surgeon or med spa for injectables, a recovery studio for contrast therapies, and either a concierge doctor or a primary care provider for labs and hormone analysis. Separate intakes and appointments, all billed and paid for separately. Some clinics have combined a few of these modalities. Most of them are not somewhere you would choose to spend a Saturday morning.

4+

The patient is the coordinator, navigating providers for care that should sit in one place.

24 of 30

Services on the LK menu that require a physician, nurse practitioner or nurse. A recovery studio without a physician can offer 6.

10,488

US medical spas as of 2023, up from 8,899 the year before. The category is commoditizing on treatment alone.

The insight

Others proved the format.

Only a licensed facility can deliver it.

SWEATHOUZ

Where a non-medical operator stops. No physician on site means no PRP, no IV therapy, no neuromodulators, no filler, no laser. A licensing threshold separates the two businesses.

Soho House

Soho Friends is a published annual tier where members buy event invitations, but no club access. Soho has proven members want medical services in the club. IV drips have been offered in London since 2022. Their Venice House opens summer 2027 with a contrast suite, cryotherapy and cold plunges. What all the California Soho House locations lack is physician led medicine.

The difference

LK was built the other way around.

The others are built around recovery and added medicine where they could. Sweathouz can’t cross the licensing line. Remedy Place and Soho House reach across it with IV drips and outside partner affiliations. A licensed medical clinic first, with the club built on top. Diagnostics, treatment rooms, an infusion suite and a physician-led team, in place before the first member walks in. They sell visits. We run stress-free care.

The offering

Built around how you want to feel.

After years running a medical practice and working on its billing side, we know medicine is organized around procedures and codes. We have watched patients try to make sense of menus written for insurers, not for them. People come in tired, sore, run down, or ready for a change. So we organized everything around five simple goals: Restore, Renew, Recover, Reset and Reconnect.

Restore

Regenerative

Six PRP protocols, therapeutic medications, a ten-drip infusion menu and NAD+ by dose.

Renew

Aesthetics

Neuromodulators and filler, RF microneedling, laser resurfacing.

Recover

Recovery

Hyperbaric oxygen, Ammortal chambers, robotic massage, compression, red light.

Reset

Diagnostics

Advanced biometrics, DEXA, DUTCH, DNA analysis. The baseline everything else is measured against.

Reconnect

The Club

The contrast suite, the Lounge, member events, and guest privileges. The reason your membership becomes part of your routine, not just your recovery.

How the ladder fills

The open clinic is the top of the funnel.

Because anyone can book a procedure without joining, every non-member treatment is a paid introduction. The conversion path runs in one direction and each step is cheap to take.

Step one

Walks in

Books a procedure or buys a day pass. Pays list price. Owes nothing further.

Step two

Becomes a Friend

$300 a year pays for itself on roughly two procedures. Low friction, high volume, and it captures the database.

Step three

Becomes a Resident

Wants the circuit and the room, not just the treatment. This is where recurring revenue begins.

Step four

Becomes Longevity

Physician-delivered programming. Hard capped. The highest retention and the highest lifetime value in the building.

Equipment strategy

Purchased where payback justifies it. Wet areas drive cost: plunges, saunas and steam carry a higher per-SF buildout than a dry medspa, which is why the lean case trims the contrast suite before it trims treatment rooms. The wet block, 800 SF: two saunas, two cold plunges and steam on a single plumbing wall, sharing that wall with the locker room. It is the first question we ask about any space.

Capacity

Capacity is counted hour by hour for each station, not assumed. Even at stabilization, every station has room to spare.

76%

Practical capacity applies a utilization ceiling to theoretical station hours, because demand concentrates at peak times and nothing runs flat out. Headroom is the growth the facility can absorb without further capital.

Aligned Downside Protection.

Ownership is priced against delivery. If the business underperforms, the investor owns more of it.

  • Investors start at 30%, priced against base-case stabilized operating income of $2.70M a year.
  • If trailing twelve-month operating income at stabilization lands below $2,200,000, ownership steps up on a straight line toward a hard cap of 40%, reached at the low case of $1,244,500.
  • At or above base case the investor stays at 30% and the founder keeps the upside. The ratchet only moves one way.
ScenarioOperating income /yrInvestor ownershipInvestor cash /yrFounder retained /yr
Low case$1,244,50040%$497,800$746,700
Base case$2,697,61130%$809,283$1,888,328
Upside case$4,150,72230%$1,245,217$2,905,505

In valuation terms the ratchet is exactly a halving of the pre-money, $11,083,333 to $7,125,000. It cushions the downside without making the investor whole: at the low case 40% of $1.24M is $497,800, still below the $809,283 that 30% of base case pays.

Investing Beyond Location One.

This round funds Marina del Rey. Pro-rata rights cover what comes after.

  • Location 1 is the proof of concept. It has to open, fill and stabilize before anything else is contemplated, and every figure in this brief describes that one building.
  • Round 1 investors receive pro-rata rights, not obligations, to invest in future locations at the same or improved terms, in proportion to their original stake. A 30% holder can maintain 30% of the platform without being required to.
  • Future locations target comparable high-income coastal and Westside markets, and only once Location 1 reaches stabilization.
  • The 25% expansion reserve on the capital page is what funds that optionality out of operating cash rather than out of a second raise. An investor who would rather take the cash can read the full-distribution column instead; the two are shown side by side because this is the actual trade.

No location beyond Marina del Rey exists today. Pro-rata rights are a mechanism, not a pipeline.

How Investors Realize Value.

Three paths, in the order they are most likely to matter.

Buyback

The company holds a right, not an obligation, to repurchase investor equity in a defined window in years 3 to 5, priced off a formula tied to trailing twelve-month operating income at a multiple agreed in the definitive documents.

Right of first refusal

If a third-party offer for the business is received, existing investors get the first right to match it before any outside sale proceeds.

Strategic sale

The primary long-term path. Multi-location platforms trade at higher multiples than single-location assets, so the value of building a second and third location is realized at exit rather than only in operating cash.

Published EBITDA multiples
  • Single location, owner is primary provider3.5x to 5.0x
  • Single location, strong operator with SOPs5.0x to 6.5x
  • Multi-location, two or more with management6.0x to 7.5x
  • Multi-location, provider bench and recurring revenue7.0x to 9.0x
  • Membership revenue premium+0.5x to 1.0x

LK runs 41.9% of revenue from memberships and access, above the 30% to 40% band that source names as a premium driver.

Multiples: Breakwater M&A, 20 February 2026. https://www.breakwaterma.com/blog/medical-spa-valuation-multiples-2026 · Industry M&A comparables, not company projections. The entry price on this round is 5.87x base-case operating income, inside the single-location band above and below every multi-location band.

What we are flagging before you ask.

  • Year 1 operating income is negative. Six of those months are construction and the rest are the opening ramp. There is no debt service to carry through it, and the $1,105,800 working capital reserve inside use of funds is sized against a modeled cash trough of $42,467 at month 9.
  • The reserve is deliberately larger than the trough it covers, 26.0 times over. With no lender there is no mandated reserve and no covenant to cure, so the cushion is a choice: it funds a slower ramp than the one modeled without a second raise. It is idle cash and we are naming it rather than leaving it to be found.
  • The ratchet cushions the downside without making the investor whole. At the low case 40% of $1.24M pays $497,800, which is still less than the $809,283 that 30% of base case pays. Every ownership percentage, valuation and buyback term in this brief is indicative and subject to definitive documents.
  • The multi-location expansion and platform exit thesis represent optionality this structure creates, not a guaranteed roadmap. No location beyond Marina del Rey currently exists, and all forward-looking multiples are sourced from industry M&A comparables, not company-specific projections.
  • Volume is flexed to 72% of base in the low case and the business still produces $1.24M of annual operating income, with fixed overhead held constant. That is the conservative treatment: in a genuine downside you would cut staff before you cut the lease.
  • All forward-looking figures are projections on the stated assumptions and are not guarantees, and actual results will differ. Market and demographic figures carry their sources, and anything we could not source was cut rather than estimated. Statements about other operators describe our understanding at the date of this brief, are drawn from public information and may change without notice. Nothing here has been audited or reviewed by an independent accountant.

Risks

What could go wrong, and what we did about it.

RiskMitigation
Membership fills slower than modeled.The clinic is open to non-members from day one, so revenue does not depend on the club filling. The low case flexes volume to 72% of base and still produces positive operating income.
Members redeem more than their fees cover.Credit banks are sized against measured redemption and the model asserts the ratio stays below 100%. The three-month minimum with 30-day change notice makes repricing operationally possible.
A key clinician leaves during the ramp.The club, recovery floor and infusion suite run on staff that are easier to hire than injectors and prescribers. A gap narrows the services offered without closing LK. As a licensed, equipped clinic, we can credential a replacement quickly, and clinical pay includes retention terms through the ramp.
The ramp is slower than modeled and cash runs short.With no loans assumed, there is no monthly payment to miss and no lender involved. Founding memberships will be sold during construction. The reserve is sized to cover a slower ramp, and the low case still reaches positive operating income at stabilization.
Wet-area construction overruns.The highest variance line in the buildout. The saunas, plunges and showers are the least predictable cost in the build. A reduced-scope plan is ready as a fallback, and the reserve gives room to absorb overruns without a second raise.
